claims.claim: GitHub is a web-based application for hosting files in repositories, collaborating on work, and tracking changes; its version tracking is powered by Git.
GitHub's browser interface can support a collaboration flow that includes creating a branch or fork, editing, committing, and creating a pull request.
GitHub Issues can plan, discuss, and track work such as bugs, features, ideas, and feedback, and can be connected to pull requests.
A pull request proposes changes from a separate branch for review before a possible merge into a base branch; later commits on that branch are added to the pull request.
Reviewers can comment, suggest changes, or request changes, and a pull request can be merged when repository requirements such as required reviews and status checks pass.
A permission authorizes a particular action, while a role is a set of permissions assigned to individuals or teams; access models vary by account type.
